evidence.title: Company values
evidence.text: # Company values At Lumen Labs, our culture has always been centered around curiosity, ownership, and moving with a healthy sense of urgency. We are a tight-knit team, and how we build [[Pulse]] is just as important as the code we ship every week. First and foremost, we believe in radical transparency. Whether we are discussing product roadmaps or reviewing infrastructure costs, open communication keeps everyone aligned. Nobody likes working in a silo, so we keep our [[Team syncs]] conversational and make sure [[Engineering guidelines]] are accessible to everyone on the team, from senior architects to our newest hires. We also champion developer autonomy. Trust is foundational here; we hire smart people and give them the space to execute without micromanagement. If someone wants to prototype a new feature or experiment with a different approach to [[Performance analytics]], they are encouraged to run with it, test it thoroughly, and share what they learn with the rest of the crew. Mistakes are treated as learning opportunities rather than failures, provided we are open about what went wrong and how to fix it. Finally, we keep our users at the center of everything. We spend a lot of time talking to engineering teams who rely on our platform day in and day out. Their pain points inform our backlog, and our shared obsession with reducing friction and latency drives us forward. As we grow [[Lumen Labs]] beyond thirty people, maintaining this collaborative and builder-first ethos is our highest priority.

evidence.title: Pulse API v2 deprecation timeline
evidence.text: # Pulse API v2 deprecation timeline Hi everyone, I'm writing to share an important update regarding our API roadmap here at Lumen Labs. As we continue to roll out improvements across Pulse, we want to make sure everyone is leveraging the most stable, performant version of our platform. To that end, please be aware that Pulse API v2 was originally scheduled for deprecation on 2026-06-01. If you are still utilizing v2 endpoints for session replay, error tracking, or performance analytics, we strongly encourage you to migrate to v3 as soon as possible. The newer version offers significant speed improvements, better payload structures, and more robust authentication methods. We have put together a comprehensive migration guide in our documentation portal to help make this transition as smooth as possible for your engineering teams. If you run into any roadblocks or have questions about specific endpoints, please don't hesitate to reach out to our support team or reply directly to this thread. Best, Noah Fischer Lumen Labs

evidence.title: Security disclosure — stored XSS in custom annotations
evidence.text: # Security disclosure — stored XSS in custom annotations Hello Lumen Labs Security Team, I am writing to report a security vulnerability I discovered in the Pulse dashboard today, February 25, 2026. Specifically, I found a stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability within the custom-annotation feature. When creating a new custom annotation, user-supplied input in the description field is insufficiently sanitized before being stored and rendered back to other dashboard users in the main session view. To reproduce this issue, you can submit an annotation payload containing standard script tags or event handlers—for example, injecting `<script>alert(document.cookie)</script>` into the annotation name or notes. When another user loads the annotated session replay, the malicious script executes within the context of their session. Please let me know if you need any additional details, request logs, or further proof-of-concept steps to verify this behavior. I will hold off on public disclosure until your team has had a chance to investigate and patch the issue. Best regards, anon.researcher1@protonmail.example

evidence.title: GDPR compliance checklist
evidence.text: # GDPR compliance checklist Review our current data handling policies ahead of the upcoming internal audit. Most of the technical safeguards are already covered by our work on [[Data Retention]] and [[Server Security]], but we need to ensure all documentation is up to date for the privacy team. Here is the standard run-down we should verify across all active services: - **Data Minimization:** Confirm that we are only collecting payload fields strictly necessary for debugging and performance monitoring. Masking rules for sensitive user input (like passwords or payment details) should be checked via [[Masking Rules]]. - **Right to Erasure:** Verify that our automated deletion scripts for user session data and error logs execute reliably within the required timeframe. Check the cron jobs handling the [[Storage Buckets]]. - **Consent and Notice:** Ensure our public-facing documentation accurately reflects what data Pulse stores, how long it persists, and [[Third-Party Subprocessors]] involved in infrastructure hosting. - **Access Controls:** Limit internal database access using role-based permissions. Only designated engineering leads should be able to query raw production payloads, as outlined in [[Internal Security Policy]]. Let's sync up during next week's standup to see who is tackling each section. If anyone needs to reference older notes, check the [[Archive Index]] or ask in the privacy channel.

evidence.title: Postmortem: Northwind missing session replays
evidence.text: # Postmortem: Northwind missing session replays We spent the morning digging into the ticket [[Northwind Retail]] opened about gaps in their [[session replay]] data. Things looked fine on our end during initial checks, but once we pulled the raw edge logs, the picture cleared up. It turns out that Northwind Retail's missing session replays were caused by an ad-blocker false-positive flagging Pulse's mobile SDK script as a tracker. Popular consumer list blocklists had recently updated their heuristic rules, which unfortunately caught our ingestion endpoint in the crossfire for a subset of end-users running strict browser extensions or device-level protection. The good news is that no data was actually corrupted or dropped on our servers; the payloads simply never made it out of the clients' devices. To prevent this from biting us again with other enterprise accounts, we need to fast-track our [[SDK proxy]] routing options and review our [[domain masking]] recommendations. I've updated [[Runbook - Adblock Mitigation]] with the specific signature patterns we found in this case so support can spot it faster next time. Let's sync during tomorrow's [[engineering standup]] to prioritize the domain fallback work.
